messages:
Mia Chen: Heads-up — after the RBAC change this morning that tightened rotator roles, we've started seeing TLS handshake failures for apac-ingress :frowning:
Tomas Alvarez: which change specifically? policy name or PR?
Mia Chen: PR #4521 removed kms:Decrypt from service-account 'cert-rotator@infra' to scope it down. I think the rotator can't unwrap keystore anymore.
Mia Chen: error from proxy logs: `tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate` followed by `kms:Decrypt denied for principal projects/…/serviceAccounts/cert-rotator@infra`
infra-bot: ALERT: 6 failed handshakes in apac-ingress in the last 5m (rule: tls.handshake.failures > 5)
Priya Singh: ugh. Can we confirm KMS denial entries in audit logs before touching IAM?
Rowan (oncall): +1 — need request IDs and which key. Mia can you paste the CloudTrail/Cloud Audit log snippet (or equivalent)?
Mia Chen: pasted audit snippet: `proto=cloudaud log=access request=projects/apac/locations/global/keyRings/rotator/cryptoKeys/cert-key method=Decrypt principal=serviceAccount:cert-rotator@infra outcome=PERMISSION_DENIED` — looks deterministic
Tomas Alvarez: mitigation path A: re-add kms:Decrypt to the cert-rotator role and restart the rotator process. B: roll back the RBAC PR if that's easier.
Priya Singh: mitigation A is fine short-term but we should do least-privilege long-term. Could we instead allow a narrow condition on the key (e.g., resource name + time window) so only the rotator can decrypt cert keys?
Mia Chen: aggree. For immediate restore I'll reapply `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` to the service account for the rotator key only.
Mia Chen: running: `gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod --member=serviceAccount:cert-rotator@infra --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter --condition='expression=resource.name.endsWith("/cryptoKeys/cert-key")'`
infra-bot: Deploy bot: RBAC patch applied to cert-rotator (change id rb-2026-03-22-01)
Rowan (oncall): After regrant, restart rotator reconcile and monitor TLS metric.
Mia Chen: done — role restored and rotator pod restarted (rotator-7f9c). Patch id rb-2026-03-22-01
Mia Chen: proxy logs now show `handshake success` for previous failing endpoints :thumbsup:
Tomas Alvarez: good. Root cause is we tightened RBAC without updating the rotator precondition matrix. We need a preflight checklist for key-dependency policies.
Priya Singh: action items: 1) immediate postmortem note, 2) add an automated IAM impact test to PRs that touch roles referenced by services, 3) enable KMS request-level audit alerting for PERMISSION_DENIED spikes, 4) add canary cert rotation test in apac region.
Mia Chen: created GH issue: redwood/infra#6789 "RBAC -> KMS dependency preflight + postmortem" and started the postmortem doc with timeline.
Rowan (oncall): Also add a metric/alert: `tls.handshake_error{region="apac"}` -> notify sec-oncall and infra-sre when > 3 in 5m. Correlate with Cloud Audit `methodName=Decrypt` AND `status=PERMISSION_DENIED`.
Tomas Alvarez: long-term: consider rotating to envelope-encryption where the rotator only needs a short-lived DEK, reduce live KMS hits during handshake.
Priya Singh: and we should enforce that any RBAC change doing privilege removal gets a 'dry run' label and run smoke checks against the services that reference that role.
Mia Chen: agreed. I'll add the smoke-check job to the RBAC PR template and add the Cloud Audit alert runbook.
infra-bot: NOTE: audit logging was temporarily spamming oncall due to alert threshold; thresholds adjusted to reduce noise.
Mia Chen: postmortem draft link: https://redwood.internal/pm/infra/6789 — will add timeline and remediation steps. Assigning follow-ups: @Tomas for IAM test, @Priya for alerts/runbook, @Rowan for oncall escalation doc.
Rowan (oncall): I'll update the runbook and add rollback play for RBAC errors.
Priya Singh: We'll also add an automated nightly canary that requests a short cert from rotator in apac and validates handshake.
Tomas Alvarez: small config suggestion: add a TLS metric tag for `rotator_key_id` so we can trace which key was involved in any handshake failure.
Mia Chen: thanks everyone. Will monitor for next 2 hours and update the postmortem. Closing the immediate incident.
Rowan (oncall): :white_check_mark: keep monitoring. If we see > 3 denies again, we'll revert to the pre-change RBAC snapshot.
Mia Chen: last check at +20m: no denies, no handshake fails. Marking incident resolved in ops channel.
